A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoomTour3D and contain complete, readable main text, Tables 1–3, Figures 1–11, and Appendices A–H. Citation renumbering and appendix reflow do not obstruct comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original supervised navigation experiments, zero-shot R2R results, modality ablations, and manual evaluation of generated trajectory descriptions in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–3, the description-quality evaluation, and appendix navigation examples.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendices B–E retain the same trajectory extraction, instruction generation, NaviLLM summarization pretraining, and navigation finetuning. Architecture, objectives, and inference procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Training sources remain RoomTour3D, CVDN, SOON, R2R, REVERIE, ScanQA, and LLaVA-23k. The same four supervised navigation benchmarks and zero-shot R2R scenario are evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain identical comparator membership, including NaviLLM, DUET, NavGPT, MapGPT, DiscussNav, LangNav, and NavCoT. The added bibliography entries introduce no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain the same splits, metrics, training mixtures, model settings, and evaluation procedures. Budgets remain 2,500 pretraining steps and 1,250 finetuning steps with batch size 256; manual evaluation still samples 100 descriptions.

E4.justification: The modality ablation in Table 2, action-data analysis, description-quality checks, and navigation case studies are unchanged. Appendices F–G retain the same qualitative examples and manually rated trajectories.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting and manual-rating summaries. Neither adds seed information, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, manual-check ratings, and qualitative findings match. Zero-shot R2R remains 14.33% SR and 10.86% SPL; description verification remains 3.08/4, with 74% rated mostly relevant or a perfect match.

T1.justification: The geometric sampling criteria, spatial/depth partitions, and mathematical reasoning are unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs that are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable geometry-aware video data, supervised navigation improvements, and trainable zero-shot navigation. Novelty and claimed benchmark advantages are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning object grounding, spatial awareness, and navigation errors are retained. Appendix H preserves the same applicability qualifications, computational-resource limitations, and future directions despite relocation.

D1.justification: The appendices retain the same preprocessing instructions, prompts, COLMAP commands, architecture details, hyperparameters, hardware, and decoding settings. Stated code/data access and licensing information are also unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds five bibliography entries, references 16–19 and 60, covering video detection, segmentation, Shot2Story, and LongVLM. These additions do not change the related-work discussion or positioning against prior navigation research.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the appendix opening by removing the CVPR-template wording and changes Xiaodan Liang’s affiliation marker from 1,2 to 1. Substantive prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 8 moves from page 17 to page 16, while Figure 9 moves upward on page 17 and surrounding appendix text reflows. The bibliography also reflows; figure content, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The methods, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, claims, and limitations are unchanged. Five bibliography additions without accompanying discussion, plus small affiliation, wording, and layout edits, produce no meaningful overall gain or loss in paper quality.
